independent_reconstruction.check: The section really assumes n>=3 and kappa>=4, full O(n) Haar and U=O_11. Eq4 is ((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+transpose O). The lemma requires Borel h and E|h(U)|<infinity. These are joint premises, not alternatives. The graph does not replace full O(n) Haar by SO(n), where the row-reflection law would fail.

With a=sqrt(kappa)+1, b=sqrt(kappa)-1, a^2+b^2=2(kappa+1), ab=kappa-1, and O^T O=I, the literal precision is (1/4)(aI-bO)^T(aI-bO). b>=0 and a-t>=2 throughout [0,b]. Reverse triangle inequality plus ||Ov||=||v|| gives the displayed lower bound. The packet correctly labels the numeric range as implicit rather than an extra author display.

The author explicitly deduces invertibility on the interval, initial positive determinant, and positivity by continuity. The lower bound excludes a nonzero kernel; finite-dimensional square injectivity implies invertibility. Continuity on the connected interval together with nonvanishing and the initial sign fixes the positive branch at b. Determinant multiplication/scaling in Eq16 gives det A=2^(-2n)(det(aI-bO))^2, hence Eq17. Positivity and Gram factorization are both needed. There is no omitted author sign proof or unsupported choice of square-root sign.

Right multiplication by O^T sends aI-bO to aO^T-bI. Multiplicativity and det O^T=det O produce the first Eq18 equality after Eq17. Transposition produces det(aO^T-bI)=det(aO-bI), the second equality. Both displayed forms and the author transpose paragraph are retained, in the correct direction.

The empty determinant convention is explicitly 1. For any chosen i in S with i>=2, D_i=I-2 e_i e_i^T is a fixed orthogonal row reflection. Full-Haar left invariance yields D_i O equal in law to O; its first row entry U is unchanged; the selected minor has exactly one negated row, hence negative determinant. These three conclusions jointly underlie the averaging argument. The graph does not confuse row and column multiplication or reverse the index condition.

The source asserts |det O_SS|<=1 and that all expectations are finite, then displays E[X]=E[X reflected]=-E[X] and concludes zero. The packet retains the bound separately and uses finite absolute expectation rather than a formal totalized integral trick. Borel h, continuous coordinates/minors, and domination by |h(U)| give actual L1 integrability. Reflected expressions are measurable and L1 by the same law (or pointwise sign and fixed-U identities). Equal-law expectation and the sign identity are both required, not alternative proof branches.

The complete expansion is over all subsets S of [n] with coefficient a^|S|(-b)^(n-|S|) times det O_SS, multiplied by 2^(-n). The complement selects diagonal entries of -bI; the sign is wholly in (-b)^(n-|S|), without a further permutation sign. Every summand is L1, so the finite sum and Eq18 signed normalization integrand are L1 and finite expectation linearity is valid. E02/E03 are legitimate implicit bookkeeping bridges, not additional author theorems.

Every subset except empty and {1} contains an index >=2 and vanishes by M11. The two possible survivors are (-b)^n E[h(U)] and a(-b)^(n-1) E[U h(U)], respectively. The packet correctly says can contribute: it does not assert these expectations are nonzero. U h(U) is L1 from the singleton bound |U|<=1. The displayed Ex55 second equality agrees exactly.

Since n>=3 in particular n>=1, (-b)^n=(-1)^(n-1)b^(n-1)(-b), while a(-b)^(n-1)=(-1)^(n-1)b^(n-1)a. Factoring gives 2^(-n)(-1)^(n-1)b^(n-1) E[(aU-b)h(U)]. Its integrand is L1 by the finite empty/singleton combination. This matches Eq15, including parity, power n-1 and denominator 2^n.
